basics.name: Ryan Donald
basics.label: Engineer
basics.summary: I am an ever curious Engineer with an interest in intelligent autonomous systems. I enjoy working on systems that can intelligently perceive and interact with the real world.

work.name: Magna Electronics
work.summary: Working on perception and tracking algorithms

work.name: Draper
highlights: Worked in a multi-disciplinary team on firmware design, implementation, and documentation, and hardware bringup and testing

work.name: Persistent Autonomy and Robot Learning (PeARL) Lab, University of Massachusetts, Lowell
work.summary: Worked for four years in a robotics research lab on multiple projects for sponsors such as DEVCOM, ONR, and Amazon
highlights: Designed, developed, and implemented a framework for underwater inspection with a robot within simulation.

Developed a predictive framework utilizing an Intel RealSense camera, attached to the wrist of a Kinova Robotics Jaco 2, mounted on a Ghost Robotics Vision 60. This allows the system to predict and react to environment motion for better target tracking during and after execution of motions within a dynamic environment.
Developed test methods and evaluation frameworks for the categorization and measurement of the autonomy of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, from both a non-contextual and contextual standpoint.
Gained experience with multiple different robots including a Fetch Robotics Mobile Manipulator, Kinova Robotics Jaco 2, Ghost Robotics Vision 60, Universal Robots UR5e, and Boston Dynamics Spot.

work.name: University of Massachusetts, Lowell
work.summary: Grader for COMP.4500 Mobile Robotics I.
highlights: Provided students in the lab with feedback and guidance during COMP.4500 Mobile Robotics I.
Graded the performance of students' robots in each of 5 lab projects during the semester.
Worked with the Professor to effectively teach students the material.
Helped teach debugging and testing principles when students' code or robots had issues.

education.area: Electrical Engineering, minor in Robotics, 3.95 GPA

publications.name: An Adaptive Framework for Manipulator Skill Reproduction in Dynamic Environments
publications.summary: An adaptive framework combining Learning from Demonstration, environment state prediction, and high-level decision making, validated on a legged mobile manipulator across 36 real-world scenarios.

publications.name: Contextual Autonomy Evaluation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles in Subterranean Environments
publications.publisher: 2023 9th International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Applications (ICARA)
publications.summary: A cascaded Fuzzy Inference System for calculating contextual autonomy scores for small Unmanned Aerial Systems, tested across seven sUAS.

publications.name: Methods for Combining and Representing Non-Contextual Autonomy Scores for Unmanned Aerial Systems
publications.publisher: 2022 8th International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Applications (ICARA)
publications.summary: Methods for combining heterogeneous autonomy features into a single score, introducing the non-contextual autonomy coordinate and autonomy distance.
